note: Bundled offline seed for the 40-week tracker. Full content is fetched from Firestore `weekContent/{week}` and cached; this file guarantees the tracker works with no network on first run. Sample weeks shown; remaining weeks follow the same schema.

weeks.babyDevelopment: The blastocyst has implanted and the amniotic sac and placenta are forming. The neural tube, which becomes the brain and spinal cord, is beginning to develop.
weeks.motherChanges: You may notice a missed period. Early signs like tender breasts and fatigue can begin. Hormone hCG is now detectable by a pregnancy test.
weeks.advice: Start a prenatal vitamin with at least 400 mcg of folic acid if you haven't already.

faqs.a: Light implantation spotting can be normal, but contact your doctor for heavy bleeding or pain.

weeks.babyDevelopment: Reflexes are developing, fingers and toes are separated, and the intestines move into the abdomen. The baby can make sucking movements.
weeks.motherChanges: Nausea often begins to ease. Your uterus is growing out of the pelvis. Risk of miscarriage drops significantly at the end of the first trimester.
weeks.advice: Your first-trimester screening/NT scan is usually done around now.

faqs.a: Many people begin to show between weeks 12 and 16, earlier in subsequent pregnancies.

weeks.babyDevelopment: You're at the halfway point. The baby is developing a regular sleep-wake pattern and can hear sounds. The anomaly scan checks organ development.
weeks.motherChanges: You may feel the first kicks (quickening). Your bump is now clearly visible.
avoid: Lying flat on your back for long periods
weeks.advice: Schedule your mid-pregnancy anomaly ultrasound if not already done.

faqs.a: Movement patterns vary. Later in pregnancy, track kicks daily and tell your doctor about reduced movement.

weeks.babyDevelopment: Eyes can open and close, and the baby can dream (REM sleep). Lungs are maturing. Welcome to the third trimester.
weeks.motherChanges: You may feel more short of breath and notice Braxton Hicks contractions. Glucose screening for gestational diabetes is common around now.
weeks.advice: Ask your doctor about the Tdap vaccine and monitoring baby's movements.

faqs.q: When should I start counting kicks?
faqs.a: Around week 28 many doctors recommend daily kick counts; use the in-app Kick Counter.
